spatial_claims.claim: AB is cut in extreme and mean ratio at C with AC the greater segment; points are collinear in order D, A, C, B
M bisects AB so AM = AB/2; AD = AM; thus h = AD = AB/2
AC = DC - DA = t - h; CB = DB - DC = u - t
t = AC + h where AC is the greater segment and h = AB/2, so by 13.1 t^2 = 5h^2
t > h because DC contains DA as a proper part (C lies between A and B)
u > t because DB contains DC as a proper part (B lies beyond C from D)

configuration_map: All points lie on a single line in order D---A---C---B. D is produced beyond A from the direction of B. M is the midpoint of AB. AD = AM = h = AB/2. DC = t = h + AC. DB = u = 3h. AC = t - h. CB = u - t. The configuration is purely one-dimensional with no angles, triangles, or circles involved. The proof proceeds through algebraic and number-theoretic reasoning about commensurability relationships among the segments.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The configuration is a simple collinear arrangement (D-A-C-B) with straightforward segment arithmetic. The core reasoning is algebraic and number-theoretic (commensurability, showing 5:1 is not a ratio of square numbers), involving no complex geometric configurations, angle decompositions, or interior/exterior arguments that could harbor hidden contradictions.
